get.description: Current session; also sets the CSRF cookie the SPA needs for POSTs.

post.description: Start a staff session. 429 with `Retry-After` once the account or IP is over its limit.

get.description: Open items per queue, for the navigation badges.
References with pair counts per status, ordered by id (keys 1-9 in the UI).

Pairs ordered proposed first, then match band high → review → low (pairs without a match
last), confidence desc, ranking score desc, reference, page. Keyset cursor over that order.

Low-band matches are hidden unless `include_low` or `band=low`. `band` (repeatable) keeps only
matches in those bands. `decided_by`: `auto` = the match row was decided automatically,
`human` = any other decided pair. `hide_removed` leaves out pages the crawler found removed.

post.description: Confirm / reject / reset ReferenceLeak rows (and the ReferenceMatch of the same pair).
Confirm / reject / reset ReferenceMatch rows (and the ReferenceLeak of the same pair).

Reject every still-proposed pair of a reference. Pairs with a fingerprint match are kept
unless `include_matches` is set.

get.description:
Clusters with at least one proposed member: linked to an original first, then by id.

`show=all` (default) lists every open cluster, linked ones first; `linked` keeps only clusters
linked to an original — most clusters are not, so that filter alone can look almost empty
(issue #2, operator 2026-09-17). `reference_id` keeps clusters linked to that original (and
implies `linked`, since a cluster unlinked to any original cannot be linked to one in
particular). `cursor` is the last item's `next_cursor` (`<linked 1|0>:<cluster id>`).

post.description:
Confirm / reject / reset members atomically. A decided member is never flipped to the
opposite decision without a reset. `reset` puts a member back to proposed (undo).
Queue availability checks for the cluster's active (non-rejected) member pages.
Merge source clusters into the target (`matching.services.merge_clusters`).
Queue availability checks for these pages at recheck priority.

get.description: Pages waiting for a safety decision, by id; `cursor` is the last page id seen.

post.description: Mark review pages clear and release their media (same service as the admin action).
Block review pages with a required reason; cancels media and deletes frame hashes.

get.description: Safety cases, open ones first, newest first. `status`: active|open|reported|settled|all.

Plain-text hotline report in German and English, for a human to copy into the form.

Only for a running case: an open one (the first report) or a reported one (a supplement, e.g.
for a mirror URL found after the report). A settled case gets 409 — it must not be reported.

post.description:
A human filed the report: record when, where and the hotline's reference (blank = none
was issued). Only an open case; corrections to a reported one go through the admin.

get.description: Queued pages by id; `cursor` is the last page id seen. Credits are computed now.

post.description:
Release queued pages for fingerprinting (reason required). All or nothing: a page with
any other safety hit, or without a customer credit any more, refuses the whole request.
Keep queued pages blocked. The decision stands on later crawls.

get.description: `needs_review` creators, newest first, each with suggestions for a possible duplicate.

post.description: It is a genuinely new creator: becomes crawlable like any other (admin's "Mark reviewed").
Merge a duplicate identity into an existing creator: never automatic, confirmation step.
The typed name is a studio/brand, not a person: record it as an alias of the target.

get.description:
Refused claims, open ones first by default, newest first.

`status`: open|resolved|dismissed|all.

post.description: Staff acted on it (e.g. rights sorted out, or the customer was told to use another file).
No follow-up needed (e.g. a false alarm from a hash-overlap threshold).

Attach a studio label (or mark not common / reject): same fields and the same
`label_common_group` service call as the admin's own form. A labeled group becomes a rebuild
anchor (`labeled_at`); it only discounts match evidence once `status=confirmed` and
`kind != not_common`.

get.description: Everything on the start page in one request (the SPA refreshes it every 60 s).
Candidates by distinct creators, then search hits (both descending), then domain.

post.description:
Approve (creates a disabled Site if absent), reject, mark hoster, ignore or reset.

Moving an approved candidate elsewhere undoes the approval: the disabled Site it created is
deleted. If that Site is enabled or already has crawl data, the request is refused (409) and
the Site is changed in the admin first.

get.description: Search provider spend and the latest calls (read-only audit log).
Every original by id, with fingerprint and review counts.
One original: all matches and leaks per page, and M2 miss reasons for its confirmed leaks.
Creators to pick from when registering an original; the first picked is the rights holder.
Organisations an original can be registered for; the uploader must pick one or none.

post.description:
Register an original from hashes computed in the browser.

Refuses (400) a document `from_json` will not validate, an unknown organisation and an unknown
or ambiguous creator;
refuses (409) a file already imported and an upload that duplicates another account's claim.
Shared-frame flags are not recomputed here - `match_references` does that at the start of
every run - and no match, leak or takedown is created or confirmed by this call.

Record why a browser run produced no hashes (issue #29 counters, input for #59).

`codec_unsupported` means the browser refused to decode the file at all, `client_failed`
every other local failure. Deliberately no file name, size or path - only the codec strings
the decoder reported, so the counts say whether cloud fingerprinting is worth building.

get.description:
Whether this browser is signed in; also sets the CSRF cookie the login POST needs.

Unauthenticated on purpose — a sign-in form has to be able to obtain a CSRF token before it has
a session. It reports only on the caller's own session and never mentions an organisation;
`GET /api/v1/app/me` is where scope is answered, and that one requires a session.

post.description:
Start a customer session. Accounts are created by the operator; there is no signup.

401 for any credential failure, 403 when the credentials were right but the account belongs to
no organisation (a staff reviewer, say — `is_staff` opens the review API, not a customer's
account), 429 once the per-account or per-IP limit is reached, with `Retry-After`.
End the session. CSRF-protected, and harmless (200) when there was no session.

Ask for a password-reset link. **The answer says nothing about the address** (ADR 0054 §2).

202 whether or not it has an account, and nothing in the body or the status differs. 429 once
the per-address or per-IP limit is reached, which tells a caller only about their own attempts.

With the flows switched off it is the **same** 202 and **no outbox row**: "off" means nothing
happens, not a different sentence (issue #153).

get.description:
Whether this link still works, and the CSRF cookie the next step needs.

404 for every reason it does not — see the module docstring. The address is named because the
link came out of that inbox: whoever holds it can set the password anyway.

post.description:
Set the new password. **Nobody is signed in** — the next step is the sign-in form.

The mailed link proves the reader has the inbox, not that they know the password they chose,
and a session minted from a link is a session a forwarded mail could have. 202 on the public
host: the password is hashed there and only the hash travels (ADR 0054 §1).

get.description:
Whether this confirmation link still works, and the CSRF cookie the button needs.

A **GET confirms nothing**: mail clients, scanners and link previews fetch links on their own,
and an address confirmed by a scanner is a confirmation nobody made. The POST below is the act.

post.description: Confirm the address. No session needed: the link was mailed to it (ADR 0054 §3).

"Send that mail again", from the banner. Signed in, so it says nothing about anybody else.

202 whether a mail went out or `RESEND_INTERVAL` swallowed it: a screen that could tell the
difference would be a screen that has to explain it. 404 while the flows are off — the same bare
answer as a route that does not exist, because for this deployment it does not.

get.description:
Who is signed in, and which organisation every other customer request is scoped to.

Also refreshes the CSRF cookie, so a session restored from a cookie can post again without
calling `GET /api/v1/app/auth/session` first.
Every original this organisation owns, one per video, newest first. No one else's.

One original with every human-reviewed matching copy, by its public id.

404 unless this organisation owns it — the same body for a malformed, unknown or foreign id.
Every page with a human-reviewed match of this organisation's originals, and its record.
One record per original something was found of. An original with nothing found has none.

One record by the original's public id: the original, its matching copies, the timeline,
and what is not known yet.

404 unless this organisation owns the original — byte-identical for a malformed, unknown or
foreign id.
An owned original with nothing found answers 200 with `case: null` and a timeline whose first
step is still pending: "nothing found" is an answer, not a missing resource.

What came down and when, newest first — living state, not an archive.

An entry can reopen: `state` is `reopened` when that URL came back, and `handled` ("no copy
online") is false whenever anything else of the same original is up again.

post.description:
Add an original to the caller's organisation from fingerprints computed in the browser.

201 created · 200 already in this account (nothing imported) · 202 received, being added
(production: the outcome follows in `GET /app/fingerprints/submissions`, including a 409 or 400
only development can decide) · 400 invalid document or missing rights declaration · 403 no
organisation · 409 needs a human check (the file or its hashes are registered elsewhere; the
answer never says where) · 413 body too large · 429 per-organisation limit, with `Retry-After`
· 503 not available on this machine (`adding_originals_unavailable`) or paused for now
(`processing_paused`, with `Retry-After`).

Count a browser run that produced no fingerprints (issue #29 counters, input for #59).

Only the decoder's words and the container type — never a file name, size or path. The answer
carries no totals: how often *other* customers fail is not a customer's business.

get.description:
Originals this organisation sent that are being added, or were in the last days.

Production accepts an upload first and adds it shortly after (202); this list is how the app
shows that, and what became of it. Empty on development, where an upload is added at once, and
for an account without an organisation.

post.description:
Declare one upload and get the chunk size to send it in.

201 created · 400 invalid, or a declaration is missing or out of date · 403 no organisation ·
404 uploads are not available on this machine · 429 per-organisation limit · 503 this account's
daily byte quota or the spool is full.

get.description: This organisation's uploads, newest first.

post.description:
Send chunk `index`, raw bytes. Re-sending the last one overwrites it; anything else is 409.

Resume by reading `next_chunk` from the upload's status and continuing there.

On the public host this is the one request that carries a customer's media, and it is
**streamed** to development and never held (`marceline/uploads/relay.py`): the body is read in
64 KiB pieces and each piece is handed on as it is read. `request.body` is not touched on that
path, which is also what keeps Django's multipart handlers — the only thing in Django that
writes an upload to a temporary file — out of it entirely.

Close the upload: the server's own digest of what it assembled must be the one sent.

400 `digest_mismatch` (the bytes on disk are not the file the customer hashed — the spool is
emptied and nothing is queued) · 409 the upload is not receiving chunks.

get.description:
One upload's state: where to resume, how far the fingerprinting has come, what it became.

This is what the add-original screen polls after the last chunk (ADR 0044 amendment
2026-09-18). `status` moves `receiving → queued → hashing → done | refused | failed`,
`frames_done`/`frames_total` are the bar (a null total means "not known yet", never a guessed
denominator), `reason` is the closed set the app has words for, `original_id` is the original
to link to once there is one, and `bytes_deleted` says whether the file is verifiably gone —
which is the only thing that entitles the screen to say it was deleted.

delete.description: Cancel an upload. The bytes go immediately; a job already being hashed is left alone.

get.description: Every issued invoice and cancellation of this organisation, newest first.

200.description: The issued invoice as stored (application/pdf, attachment).

get.description:
The stored PDF of one issued document, by its public id.

404 unless this organisation's and issued — the same body for a malformed, integer, unknown,
draft or foreign id.

Claimant, partners, the rights status of every owned original, and uploaded proofs.

A signed-in account without an organisation has nothing to declare: 404.

put.description:
Choose the claimant type. 409 `claimant_type_locked` once staff checked documents.

202 on production: accepted into the outbox, applied by development shortly.

post.description:
Issue a new account-control token (replaces the previous one).

202 on production: accepted into the outbox, applied by development shortly.

Self-declare one original. 409 with a code when incomplete, outdated or not open.

202 on production: accepted into the outbox — production's local tables carry no originals, so
whether `original_id` is really this organisation's is checked when development applies it, not
here. Applied by development shortly.

Withdraw this original's self-declaration (back to unverified), with a reason.

409 `declaration_not_withdrawable` unless the record is self_declared: once staff received
documents or verified it, only staff change it. 202 on production: accepted into the outbox,
applied by development shortly (see `declare_work` on why the existence check waits for it).

Declare that the documents on file give this organisation the right or authority it
declared for this original (ADR 0034 amendment 2026-09-18).

Only the customer may make this statement — staff record that the documents are formally
complete and nothing more — so there is no staff route to it anywhere. 409
`authority_not_declarable` unless the record is documents_complete, 409
`declaration_version_outdated` when the wording has changed since the page was loaded.

202 on production: accepted into the outbox, applied by development shortly (see
`declare_work` on why the existence check waits for it).

Take that statement back, with a reason (back to documents_complete). The documents stay
on file; only the customer's statement about them goes.

409 `authority_not_withdrawable` unless the record is authority_declared. 202 on production:
accepted into the outbox, applied by development shortly.

Add a licensed partner. 409 `invalid_domain`, `partner_domain_required`, … when refused.

202 on production: accepted into the outbox, applied by development shortly.

Affirm there are no licensed partners. 409 `partners_exist` while any is listed.

202 on production: accepted into the outbox, applied by development shortly.

delete.description:
Remove one of this organisation's partners. Anyone else's: 404.

202 on production: accepted into the outbox — the local table carries no partners, so whether
`partner_id` is really this organisation's is checked when development applies it. Applied by
development shortly.

post.description:
Upload a rights-relevant document excerpt (PDF, PNG or JPEG) — never media.

It is stored encrypted and read by staff only. 413 too large, 415 not a PDF/PNG/JPEG,
503 while the vault is not configured.

get.description:
Every confirmed finding of this record, with its notice-gate blockers and suggested
provider/channel — what the "Prepare notice draft" screen builds its per-URL list from.
Every notice draft of this organisation, newest first.

post.description:
Prepare a draft for one recipient and channel, grouping the selected findings.

409 `finding_not_eligible` (with the blockers per page id) when any selected URL is not
currently eligible; the customer drops it from the selection and tries again. 409
`unknown_channel` when `complaint_channel_id` is not a channel the directory offers for this
host any more, and 409 `unknown_recipient` when `recipient.hostname` is not a host of the
selected findings — the screen refetches the candidates and picks again.

202 on production: accepted into the outbox — the findings, the matches and the provider
directory live on development, so whether this draft may be prepared at all is decided when
development applies it, and the outcome appears in `GET /app/notices/submissions`.

get.description:
Notice writes this organisation sent that are being applied, or were in the last days.

Production accepts a notice write and development applies it a minute later (ADR 0046); this
list is how the app shows that, and what became of it — including a refusal only development
can decide, because only it holds the findings, the gate and the draft's state. Empty on
development, where a write is applied at once, and for an account without an organisation.

200.description: The approved notice as a file (attachment): the text itself, an unsent .eml message, or the evidence annex.

get.description:
Download the approved notice: `txt` (the exact approved text), `eml` (an unsent message to
open in the customer's own mail program) or `annex` (the evidence annex).

Nothing is transmitted here — the file is bytes for the browser, and `sandbox_send` stays the
only path that hands a draft to a mail transport. An unknown format is the same 404 as an
unknown id. 409 `not_approved` before the confirmations are made (an export may never be a
way past them) and `already_closed` for a withdrawn or corrected draft.

On production the bytes come from the signed bundle (`_export_from_cache`): a download is the
one customer read whose record is a write, so the view mediates it instead of the cache
middleware — it takes the document and appends one `notice_exported` outbox item, which is how
the `exported` event reaches the append-only log on development.

post.description:
Confirm every required declaration and freeze the exact rendered text.

409 `confirmation_incomplete` (with the missing kinds) or `finding_no_longer_eligible` (with
the blockers per page id) when the world changed since the draft was created.

202 on production: accepted into the outbox. The eligibility re-check and the text freeze need
the findings and the gate, which live on development, so it happens when development applies
the write — a draft that stopped being eligible in the meantime is refused there, and the
refusal appears in `GET /app/notices/submissions`.

"I sent this myself." 409 `sandbox_cannot_mark_real_send` for a sandbox organisation.

202 on production: accepted into the outbox, applied by development shortly. Marceline still
sends nothing here or anywhere else — this only records what the customer did.

Sandbox organisations only: an email copy to a `NOTICE_SANDBOX_RECIPIENTS` address.

409 `not_sandbox`, `recipient_not_allowlisted`, or `not_approved`.
Record what the provider answered. 202 on production: accepted into the outbox.
Take a notice back. 202 on production: accepted into the outbox.

Close this draft as `corrected` and open a fresh one with the same findings, to redo.

202 on production: accepted into the outbox; the successor appears in the list once
development has applied it.

200.description: Everything this organisation registered and everything we recorded for it, as one JSON document (attachment) — the same document `manage.py export_customer_data` writes to a file.

get.description:
Download this organisation's own export: their own API documents, their originals'
fingerprints, and their notice drafts — `export_document`, streamed as a file.

404 for a signed-in account with no organisation (there is nothing to export — the same rule
`GET /app/rights` uses). 429, with `Retry-After`, once more than one export has been requested
in the rolling hour.

Where this redemption stands, and the CSRF cookie every step after it needs.

404 for every reason a token does not work — see the module docstring.

post.description: Step one. Django's own validators decide; the username is the address on the invite.

Step two: both versioned wordings, stored verbatim with their versions.

The *Unternehmer* declaration (§ 14 BGB, issue #92) and the declaration of majority and full
legal capacity (issue #123). Two ticks, one step, one moment — and an unticked one is named, so
somebody who missed a box is told which.

The evidence behind the first stays a staff step (issue #92): a tick converts nobody, and the
screen says so rather than pretending the account is finished. The second is a declaration by
decision and not a verification: **no date of birth is asked for and no document is accepted**.

A version the screen displayed that is no longer current answers `declaration_version_outdated`
— the same code the rights declarations use. The screen reloads and shows today's wording.

Step three: the pilot agreement and the service privacy notice, one acceptance row each.

`documents_not_published` while `ONBOARDING_DOCUMENTS` is empty — the gate that keeps this
flow behind the legal work. It is a problem code, not a token refusal: the token is fine and
the person should be told to come back, not shown the neutral page.

Step four: the EU-only scope (issue #95 item 7).

A country outside the EU answers 200 with `outside_eu` set — the screen ends politely and no
account is created. **The invite is not consumed** and only a count is kept, never which
country it was (ADR 0052 §5): a typo on a select box must not cost somebody their invitation.

The last step: the account appears and the browser is signed in (ADR 0052 §8).

`business_status_not_evidenced` when the operator has set the issue #92 guard to `refuse` — the
honest answer is that the account is being set up by hand, and the invite stays open so that
the same link finishes the job once staff have recorded the evidence.

**On production nothing is created**: the redemption goes into the outbox and the answer is 202
(ADR 0052 §9). The creator is told the account is being set up, never that it exists, and the
browser is not signed in — there is no account to sign in to yet.

get.description: Which accounts this organisation has claimed, and the code of an open claim.

post.description:
Claim one platform account and get the code to place. Claiming it again gives a new code.

A platform that runs no identity check of its own gets **no code** (`code_accepted` false): a
code in that page's bio could not establish who the creator is, so staff arrange a video call.

409 with a code for a handle or link we will not store (`invalid_handle`, `host_not_allowed`,
`url_not_accepted_for_platform`). 202 on production: accepted into the outbox.

"I have placed the code." Nothing is verified by it; a person still has to look.

409 `code_expired` once the code has run out — claim the account again for a fresh one.
202 on production: accepted into the outbox, where the claim is resolved by development.

get.description: This organisation's own requests, with the deadline and the address answering them.

post.description:
Ask for a copy of everything this organisation's account holds (Art. 15, Art. 20).

409 `already_open` when one is already open, which the screen reads as "we have it".
202 on production: accepted into the outbox, recorded on development a minute later.

Ask for this organisation's data to be deleted and the pilot to end (Art. 17).

The typed word is checked **here and again on development**, because the write may travel
through the outbox and the second machine must not take a deletion request on trust. 409
`confirmation_mismatch` when it does not match, `already_open` when one is already open.

It still deletes nothing: a staff member sets the end date (ADR 0045), the retention window runs
from there, and until then the creator can withdraw the request.
Take back the open export request. 409 `not_open` when there is none.

Take back the open deletion request while it is still open. 409 `not_open` when there is
none — which is also what another organisation's open request gets, because this only ever
looks at the caller's own.

the rights declarations (`marceline/rights/services.py`).

profile_url.title: Profile Url

state.description: pending: a code is waiting. placed: you told us it is up. expired: the code ran out — ask for a new one.
state.title: State

code.description: The one-time code to place, while one is live. Null once the claim is settled.
code.title: Code

method.description: How it was established, once it was. Null otherwise.
method.title: Method

label.description: The platform's own name, not a translated word.
label.title: Label

hosts.description: The only hosts a profile link may name. Empty: this platform takes no link.
hosts.title: Hosts

code_accepted.description: Whether a placed code can settle a claim on this platform. False where the platform runs no identity check of its own before publication (ADR 0055): no code is issued there and staff arrange a short video call instead.
code_accepted.title: Code Accepted

identity_status.description: The organisation's identity check — the same field the notice gate reads.
identity_status.title: Identity Status

method.description: How it was established. `staff_legacy`: recorded by staff outside this flow.
method.title: Method

code_ttl_hours.description: How long a code stays usable.
code_ttl_hours.title: Code Ttl Hours

VerificationWriteAcceptedOut.description:
Production's answer to a write it cannot apply itself (ADR 0028 write path): accepted into
the outbox, applied by development shortly. The screen says so and shows no code yet — the code
is generated where the record lives and arrives with the next read.
VerificationWriteAcceptedOut.title: VerificationWriteAcceptedOut

status.description: requested: we have it. in_progress: somebody is working on it. done: it was answered. withdrawn: you took it back.
status.title: Status

due_at.description: When the answer is due at the latest (Art. 12(3) GDPR, one month).
due_at.title: Due At

settled_at.description: When it was answered or withdrawn. Null while it is open.
settled_at.title: Settled At

DataRequestsOut.description: Everything the screen needs, including the words it must not invent itself.

contact_email.description: Where a request is answered from, and where one can also simply be written.
contact_email.title: Contact Email

deletion_phrase.description: The word a deletion request has to echo, the same in every language.
deletion_phrase.title: Deletion Phrase

DataRequestsOut.title: DataRequestsOut

DataRequestAcceptedOut.description:
Production's answer to a write it cannot apply itself (ADR 0028 write path): accepted into
the outbox, applied by development shortly. The screen says so and never says "done".
DataRequestAcceptedOut.title: DataRequestAcceptedOut

confirm.description: Must equal `deletion_phrase` exactly. Deleting cannot be undone, so the request is not taken from a single press of a button.
confirm.title: Confirm
